newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Seasonal factors widen NZ qtrly c/a deficit - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Seasonal factors widen NZ qtrly c/a deficit - SNZ.

text.p: Seasonal factors influenced the NZ$789 million deterioration between the March and June 1996 quarter current account deficits, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
The June quarter deficit was NZ$836 million, compared with a March quarter deficit of NZ$47 million.

The surplus balance on merchandise trade improved by $493 million to $740 million from the March to June quarters. The improvement was more than offset by a $1.28 billion deterioration in the balance on invisibles, to a deficit of $1.58 billion.

June quarter merchandise exports were higher than usual, with a seasonally high level of dairy exports contributing. This follows a lower than usual merchandise trade export result for the March quarter.
SNZ said the main effect on the invisibles balance was a seasonally driven fall in travel receipts, from a fall in the number of overseas visitors.

A decline in net investment income, resulting from a rise in income accruing to overseas investors and lower returns from New Zealand's investments overseas, also contributed to the invisibles decline.

After showing relative improvement over the period from the June to December 1995 quarters, the trend estimate of the current account balance has now resumed the long-term fall evident since the September 1993 quarter, SNZ said.
The current account deficit for the year ended June 1996 was NZ$3.66 billion, unchanged from the March year and a $114 million improvement from the June 1995 year.
At 4.1 percent of GDP, the June year deficit was little changed from the 4.2 percent GDP ratio for the March year.
